States and diagrams

Dome computes the properties of a state from two independent properties, with values shifted to the reference states of the Moran and Shapiro tables. This page follows the second example, Help › Examples › States and properties (water).

Agreement with the tables

Enthalpy, internal energy and entropy are shifted to the reference states of the Moran and Shapiro tables. Differences between states, and the cycle results built from them, agree closely with the tables; a single value can differ from the printed table by about 1 kJ/kg, and by up to about 5 kJ/kg in parts of the superheated tables. Answers graded in ENES232 use the printed tables.

Fluids

A fluid line sets the fluid for the state lines after it: water, r134a, r22, ammonia, propane or air. Air is an ideal gas with variable specific heats, as in Table A-22. A state of another fluid names it in parentheses: state 2 (r134a) : ….

State lines

fluid water
p_b = 15 [bar]
state 1 : p = p_b, T = 50 [C]
state 2 : p = p_b, x = 0.3
state 3 : p = p_b, h = 2200 [kJ/kg]
state 4 : p = p_b, T = T_4
  • state L : a = …, b = … fixes state L from two of p, T, v, u, h, s and x, and defines p_L, T_L, v_L, u_L, h_L, s_L and x_L. A label may be a number or a name such as 2s.
  • The two values may be numbers, variables or expressions, and may be unknowns found by the rest of the sheet.
  • A pair that does not fix a state is refused with the reason: values outside the property data, p and T together on the saturation line, and pairs that fit more than one state.

Property functions

A property function gives one property at a state that need not be numbered: h(water, p = p_b, x = 0). The functions are p, T, v, u, h, s, x, cp, cv and rho, and Tsat(water, p = …) and psat(water, T = …) give saturation values. Unknowns may sit inside them.

The states table

The States tab of the results lists the phase and properties of every state in the units chosen in the header. The two properties given on each state line are in bold. The copy button at the right of the tab's header copies the table as tab-separated text, and File › Export › States table writes it as a CSV file.

Diagrams

A plot line draws a property diagram of states of the sheet: Ts, pv, ph or hs. Between two state labels, a path names the property held constant.

PathProcess
-p-, -s-, -T-, -v-, -h-At constant pressure, entropy, temperature, specific volume or enthalpy. Drawn dashed when that property differs between the two states, as for an expansion with a turbine efficiency.
--A straight line.
 
plot Ts : 1 -p- 2 -p- 3 -p- 4
plot ph : 1 -p- 2 -p- 3 -p- 4

Each plot line is one figure, with its own tab in the figure pane. The buttons in the pane's header zoom to a box, fit the view to the data, show data tips and export the figure. The boxes under the figure show or hide the previous run, the saturation dome, and the isobars or isotherms.

Dragging a state

A state can be dragged along an axis of the figure when the property it is given on that axis is an input of the sheet. An input is a line name = number [unit], or a number written in a state line (x = 0 in state 3 makes x_3 an input), so T = T_4 with T_4 = 320 [C] qualifies, and so does T = 320 [C] written in the state line. A ring marks each such state. The new value is written where the number stands, and the sheet is solved again.

The previous run

After an input changes, Dome shows what changed: the edited line is tinted and shows the previous value, values that changed show the change beside them, the changed variables and states are tinted in the Workspace and the states table, and figures draw the previous run dashed with a legend naming the input that changed. Below, the boiler pressure p_b of the second example was changed from 15 bar to 30 bar.
